Let
\[
X_i=T_i-I\qquad (i=1,2,3).
\]
Since \(n\) is a power of \(p\), over \(\mathbb F_p\),
\[
T_i^n-I=(1+X_i)^n-1=X_i^n.
\]
Thus the shift module is modeled by
\[
R=\mathbb F_p[x,y,z]/(x^n,y^n,z^n),
\]
with \(x,y,z\) corresponding to \(X_1,X_2,X_3\).

Put
\[
u=x+y+z.
\]
Because \(n\) is a \(p\)-power, the linear change of variables \((x,y,z)\mapsto(u,y,z)\) preserves the truncated form:
\[
R\cong \mathbb F_p[u,v,w]/(u^n,v^n,w^n).
\]
The condition
\[
(T_1+T_2+T_3-3I)f=0
\]
is simply
\[
uf=0,
\]
so
\[
f=u^{n-1}g(v,w),
\qquad
g\in S:=\mathbb F_p[v,w]/(v^n,w^n).
\]

On this subspace we may set \(x=-v-w,\ y=v,\ z=w\). Since \(q\) is a \(p\)-power,
\[
x^q=-(v^q+w^q),\qquad y^q=v^q,\qquad z^q=w^q.
\]
Let \(r=v^q,\ t=w^q\). Then
\[
A=xy+yz+zx \text{ at } q\text{-level}=-(r^2+rt+t^2),
\]
\[
B=xyz \text{ at } q\text{-level}=-rt(r+t),
\]
and
\[
C=(x^q-y^q)(y^q-z^q)(z^q-x^q).
\]

Now extend scalars to a field containing a primitive cube root of unity \(\omega\). This does not change dimension. Diagonalize the cyclic permutation by coordinates \(\xi,\eta\) on the plane \(x+y+z=0\), so that the cyclic action has eigenvalues \(\omega,\omega^2\). Then
\[
S\cong K[\xi,\eta]/(\xi^n,\eta^n),
\]
and a monomial \(\xi^i\eta^j\) is cyclically invariant exactly when
\[
i\equiv j\pmod 3.
\]

In these coordinates,
\[
xy+yz+zx\sim \xi\eta,
\]
\[
r^2+rt+t^2=(xy+yz+zx)^q\sim \xi^q\eta^q.
\]
Hence
\[
D^{(q-1)/2}A\sim (\xi\eta)^{(q-1)/2}\xi^q\eta^q
=\xi^L\eta^L,
\]
where
\[
L=\frac{3q-1}{2}.
\]

Also \(B\) and \(C\) become two independent linear combinations of \(\xi^{3q}\) and \(\eta^{3q}\). Therefore the conditions \(Bg=0\) and \(Cg=0\) are equivalent to
\[
\xi^{3q}g=0,\qquad \eta^{3q}g=0.
\]

So a monomial \(\xi^i\eta^j\) survives exactly when
\[
i\ge n-3q=(p-3)q,\qquad j\ge (p-3)q,
\]
and
\[
i\ge n-L \quad\text{or}\quad j\ge n-L.
\]
Set
\[
a=(p-3)q,\qquad h=n-L.
\]
Inside the square \(a\le i,j\le n-1\), shift \(i=a+I,\ j=a+J\). Then
\[
0\le I,J\le 3q-1,
\]
and the final condition becomes
\[
\max(I,J)\ge h-a=\frac{3q+1}{2}.
\]
The congruence condition remains \(I\equiv J\pmod 3\).

There are \(q\) integers of each residue class modulo \(3\) in \(\{0,\dots,3q-1\}\), so the total congruent pairs are
\[
3q^2.
\]
We subtract the pairs with
\[
0\le I,J<\frac{3q+1}{2}.
\]
Since \(q\) is odd, among these \((3q+1)/2\) integers the residue counts are
\[
\frac{q+1}{2},\quad \frac{q+1}{2},\quad \frac{q-1}{2}.
\]
Thus the excluded number is
\[
2\left(\frac{q+1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{q-1}{2}\right)^2
=\frac{3q^2+2q+3}{4}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\dim_{\mathbb F_p}V_n
=3q^2-\frac{3q^2+2q+3}{4}
=\frac{9q^2-2q-3}{4}.
\]

Since \(q=n/p\), the final answer is
\[
\boxed{\frac{9(n/p)^2-2(n/p)-3}{4}}.
\]
